note: Draft recipes for development, written from the analysis examples. A dietitian must write and sign the real collection; production refuses this file. Amounts are for the whole dish, never per person. Steps carry no amounts. RCP-0.2.0 (16 Oct 2026): 69 more development recipes so that each food has several dishes (dals, khichdi, chilla, upma, pulao and sabjis for every vegetable in the food list). Names, amounts and steps are drafts for the dietitian to rewrite. Moong dal halwa is included only so that a request for it is answered honestly: it is a sweet, and the Golden Rules do not allow a sweet as a home-meal dish.

recipes.name: Aloo Pyaz ki Sabji (dry, light)
steps: Heat the oil, add jeera, then the sliced onion; cook till soft.
Add the cubed potato with haldi, dhania powder, chilli powder and salt, and a splash of water.
Cover and cook for 12 to 15 minutes till the potato is soft, stirring now and then.
recipes.why_it_fits: Dry preparation keeps the oil low.

recipes.name: Bhindi Sabji (dry)
steps: Wash the bhindi and dry it fully, then cut it into small pieces.
Heat the oil, add jeera, then the onion; cook till soft.
Add the bhindi, haldi, dhania powder and chilli powder; cook uncovered on low heat, stirring gently, till tender.
Add salt at the end so the bhindi stays crisp.
recipes.why_it_fits: Fibre-rich and cooked with little oil.

recipes.name: Aloo Gobhi (dry)
steps: Heat the oil, add jeera and the grated ginger.
Add the cauliflower florets and cubed potato with haldi, dhania powder, chilli powder and salt.
Cover and cook on low heat for 15 to 20 minutes till both are soft, stirring now and then.
recipes.why_it_fits: Mixes a starchy vegetable with a fibre-rich one.

recipes.name: Lauki Chana Dal
steps: Soak the chana dal for an hour.
Pressure-cook the dal with the cubed lauki, haldi and salt till soft.
Heat the oil, add jeera, the chopped tomato and chilli powder; cook till soft and pour over the dal.
recipes.why_it_fits: Filling, with protein from the dal.

recipes.name: Cabbage Matar Sabji
steps: Heat the oil, add jeera and the slit green chilli.
Add the shredded cabbage, peas, haldi and salt; mix well.
Cover and cook on low heat for about 10 minutes till just soft.
recipes.why_it_fits: Mostly fibre-rich vegetables, cooked with little oil.

recipes.name: Palak Sabji (dry)
steps: Wash and chop the palak.
Heat the oil, add jeera, garlic and the onion; cook till soft.
Add the palak, chilli powder and salt; cook uncovered till the water dries.
recipes.why_it_fits: A fill-up green vegetable, cooked dry.

recipes.name: Moong Dal Tadka
steps: Pressure-cook the moong dal with haldi and salt till soft.
Heat the ghee, add jeera, garlic, onion and tomato; cook till soft.
Pour the tadka over the dal and mix.
recipes.why_it_fits: Protein from the dal, with a small tadka.

recipes.name: Palak Paneer Bhurji
steps: Heat the oil, add jeera and the chopped tomato; cook till soft.
Add the chopped palak and cook till wilted.
Crumble in the paneer with salt and mix for a few minutes.
recipes.why_it_fits: Vegetables with protein from paneer.

recipes.name: Moong Dal Khichdi
steps: Wash the moong dal and rice together.
Pressure-cook them with haldi, salt and plenty of water till soft and mushy.
Heat the oil, add jeera, and pour it over the khichdi; mix well.
recipes.why_it_fits: A one-pot meal with protein from the dal.

recipes.name: Moong Dal Chilla
steps: Soak the moong dal for three hours, then grind it with the green chilli, jeera and salt into a smooth batter.
Heat a flat pan with a little oil and spread a ladle of batter thin.
Cook both sides till golden and serve hot.
recipes.why_it_fits: High in protein and cooked with very little oil.

recipes.name: Moong Dal Soup
steps: Pressure-cook the moong dal with the tomato, haldi and salt till very soft.
Mash lightly and add water to get a thin soup.
Heat the oil, add jeera, pour it over the soup and simmer for a few minutes.
recipes.why_it_fits: Light and easy to digest.

recipes.name: Palak Moong Dal
steps: Pressure-cook the moong dal with haldi and salt till soft.
Heat the oil, add jeera and the tomato; cook till soft, then add the chopped palak till wilted.
Mix the palak into the dal and simmer for five minutes.
recipes.why_it_fits: Iron-rich greens with protein from the dal.

recipes.name: Lauki Moong Dal
steps: Pressure-cook the moong dal with the cubed lauki, haldi and salt till soft.
Heat the oil, add jeera and the tomato; cook till soft.
Pour it over the dal and mix.
recipes.why_it_fits: A light, filling dal with plenty of fibre.

recipes.name: Jain Moong Dal Tadka
steps: Pressure-cook the moong dal with haldi and salt till soft.
Heat the oil, add jeera, the green chilli and the tomato; cook till soft.
Pour the tadka over the dal and mix.
recipes.why_it_fits: Protein from the dal, made the Jain way.

recipes.name: Moong Dal Halwa (lighter)
steps: Soak the moong dal for three hours and grind it coarse.
Roast it in the ghee on low heat, stirring all the time, till golden and fragrant.
Add hot water and the sugar and cook till the ghee separates; top with chopped almonds.
recipes.why_it_fits: A sweet: the programme asks to have sweets less often, so this is only for a special occasion.

recipes.name: Toor Dal Tadka
steps: Pressure-cook the toor dal with haldi and salt till soft, then mash lightly.
Heat the oil, add jeera, the tomato and chilli powder; cook till soft.
Pour the tadka over the dal and simmer for five minutes.
recipes.why_it_fits: Protein from the dal, with a small tadka.

recipes.name: Toor Dal with Drumstick
steps: Pressure-cook the toor dal with the drumstick pieces, haldi and salt till soft.
Heat the oil, add jeera, the tomato and chilli powder; cook till soft.
Mix the tadka into the dal and simmer for five minutes.
recipes.why_it_fits: Fibre from the drumstick and protein from the dal.

recipes.name: Toor Dal Lauki
steps: Pressure-cook the toor dal with the cubed lauki, haldi and salt till soft.
Heat the oil, add jeera and the tomato; cook till soft.
Mix the tadka into the dal.
recipes.why_it_fits: A light dal with plenty of fibre.

recipes.name: Masoor Dal
steps: Wash the masoor dal and cook it with haldi and salt till soft; it needs no soaking.
Heat the oil, add jeera, the tomato and chilli powder; cook till soft.
Pour the tadka over the dal and mix.
recipes.why_it_fits: Quick to cook, with protein and fibre.

recipes.name: Masoor Dal Palak
steps: Cook the masoor dal with haldi and salt till soft.
Heat the oil, add jeera and the chopped palak; cook till wilted.
Mix the palak into the dal and simmer for five minutes.
recipes.why_it_fits: Greens and lentils together.

recipes.name: Chana Dal Tadka
steps: Soak the chana dal for an hour, then pressure-cook it with haldi and salt till soft.
Heat the oil, add jeera, the tomato and chilli powder; cook till soft.
Pour the tadka over the dal and mix.
recipes.why_it_fits: High in fibre and protein.

recipes.name: Rajma Masala
steps: Soak the rajma overnight, then pressure-cook it with salt till soft.
Heat the oil, add jeera, then the onion; cook till golden.
Add the tomato, haldi, dhania powder and chilli powder; cook till the oil separates.
Add the rajma with a little of its water and simmer for fifteen minutes.
recipes.why_it_fits: High in fibre and protein.

recipes.name: Jain Rajma
steps: Soak the rajma overnight, then pressure-cook it with salt till soft.
Heat the oil, add jeera, the tomato, haldi, dhania powder and chilli powder; cook till the oil separates.
Add the rajma with a little of its water and simmer for fifteen minutes.
recipes.why_it_fits: Rajma made the Jain way.

recipes.name: Chana Masala
steps: Soak the chickpeas overnight, then pressure-cook them with salt till soft.
Heat the oil, add jeera, then the onion; cook till golden.
Add the tomato, haldi, dhania powder and chilli powder; cook till the oil separates.
Add the chickpeas with a little of their water and simmer for fifteen minutes.
recipes.why_it_fits: High in fibre and protein.

recipes.name: Chana Palak
steps: Soak the chickpeas overnight, then pressure-cook them with salt till soft.
Heat the oil, add jeera and the tomato; cook till soft, then add the palak till wilted.
Add the chickpeas and simmer for ten minutes.
recipes.why_it_fits: Fibre and iron-rich greens together.

recipes.name: Lobia Masala
steps: Soak the lobia for four hours, then pressure-cook it with salt till soft.
Heat the oil, add jeera, then the onion; cook till soft.
Add the tomato, haldi and chilli powder; cook till mushy.
Add the lobia and simmer for ten minutes.
recipes.why_it_fits: High in fibre and protein.

recipes.name: Lobia with Lauki
steps: Soak the lobia for four hours, then pressure-cook it with the cubed lauki, haldi and salt till soft.
Heat the oil, add jeera and the tomato; cook till soft.
Mix the tadka into the lobia and simmer for five minutes.
recipes.why_it_fits: Light, with fibre from both.

recipes.name: Tofu Bhurji
steps: Crumble the tofu.
Heat the oil, add jeera, then the capsicum and tomato; cook till soft.
Add the tofu with haldi, chilli powder and salt and cook for five minutes.
recipes.why_it_fits: High in protein.

recipes.name: Tofu Capsicum Sabji
steps: Cut the tofu into cubes and the capsicum into strips.
Heat the oil, add jeera and the capsicum; cook for a few minutes.
Add the tofu with haldi, chilli powder and salt and cook gently for five minutes.
recipes.why_it_fits: Protein with a crunchy vegetable.

recipes.name: Besan Chilla
steps: Mix the besan with water, salt and jeera into a smooth batter, then stir in the chopped onion, tomato and green chilli.
Heat a flat pan with a little oil and spread a ladle of batter thin.
Cook both sides till golden and serve hot.
recipes.why_it_fits: High in protein and cooked with very little oil.

recipes.name: Vegetable Khichdi
steps: Wash the moong dal and rice together.
Pressure-cook them with the carrot, peas, cauliflower, haldi, salt and plenty of water till soft.
Heat the oil, add jeera, and pour it over the khichdi; mix well.
recipes.why_it_fits: A one-pot meal with vegetables and protein.

recipes.name: Vegetable Pulao
steps: Wash the rice.
Heat the oil, add jeera, then the onion; cook till soft, then add the peas and carrot for two minutes.
Add the rice, haldi, salt and water, cover and cook on low heat till the rice is done.
recipes.why_it_fits: Rice with vegetables.

recipes.name: Vegetable Upma
steps: Dry-roast the suji on low heat till fragrant and set it aside.
Heat the oil, add jeera, then the onion and green chilli; cook till soft, then add the carrot and peas.
Add water and salt, bring to a boil, then stir in the suji and cook till it absorbs the water.
recipes.why_it_fits: A light breakfast-style dish with vegetables.

recipes.name: Lemon Rice
steps: Cook the rice till each grain is separate and let it cool a little.
Heat the oil, add jeera, the peanuts, green chilli and haldi; stir for a minute.
Mix this into the rice with salt and the lemon juice.
recipes.why_it_fits: A simple rice dish.

recipes.name: Capsicum Aloo Sabji
steps: Wash and cut the capsicum into small pieces.
Heat the oil, add jeera.
Add the capsicum with haldi, dhania powder, chilli powder and salt, and a splash of water.
Cover and cook on low heat till tender, stirring now and then.

recipes.why_it_fits: Protein from the paneer with a crunchy vegetable.

recipes.name: Baingan Bharta
steps: Roast the whole brinjal on a flame or in the oven till the skin is charred and the flesh is soft, then peel and mash it.
Heat the oil, add jeera, then the onion; cook till soft, then add the tomato, haldi and chilli powder.
Add the mashed brinjal and salt and cook for five minutes.
recipes.why_it_fits: Roasting instead of frying keeps the oil low.

Heat the oil, add jeera, then the onion; cook till golden.
Add the greens, haldi and salt and simmer for ten minutes.
recipes.why_it_fits: Leafy greens with fibre and iron, with less oil than the traditional dish.

Add the drumstick, salt and a little water, cover and cook till tender.
recipes.why_it_fits: A light curry with fibre.

recipes.name: Raw Banana Sabji

recipes.why_it_fits: Light, with protein from the peas.

recipes.name: Lettuce and Cucumber Salad
steps: Wash and chop the lettuce, cucumber and tomato.
Toss them with the lemon juice and salt just before serving.
recipes.why_it_fits: Raw vegetables, with nothing cooked.
